LESSON PLAN CREATIVE ARTS ACTIVITIES
 Week: Lesson:
 SCHOOL GRADE DATE TIME ROLL
 TWO
STRAND: PAPER CRAFT
SUB STRAND: FORMS: Curling technique: make curled paper items freely
SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES
By the end of the lessons, the learner should be able to:-
  Identify sample paper item made using the curling method for fun and motivation.
  Experiment with tools and materials used in making curled paper decoration for beauty and self –expression.
KEY INQUIRIES QUESTION
  Have ever seen items using curled paper?
  How do you make curled paper items?
  Would you want to make decorations using curled papers?
  How would you want your curled paper items to be used?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and collaboration  Respect Self-esteem
  Self-efficacy  Sharing Self-awareness
  Creativity and imagination  responsibility
 Health and hygiene
Learning Resources
Papers, pair of scissors, cutting blades,
Pencils, rulers, adhesive ,
KLB Visionary art and craft Grade 2 Teachers Guide pg. 96-99
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pair/groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT
Step 1: Display to learner’s sample of curled paper items.
Step 2: Provide and assortment of papers to learners and Guide learners on curling method of paper craft.
Step 3: Guide learners into carrying out the curling.
Step 4: Learners to observe safety measures.
SUMMARY
The art of curling paper involves raisin flat paper into various shapes.
CONCLUSION
Learners to display their work and talk about others work.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Learners to undertake a community project to collect re-usable waste paper from their community for use in paper
activities.
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON/SELF-REMARKS

SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES
By the end of the lessons, the learner should be able to:-
  Identify sample paper items made using the pleating method for fun and motivation.
  Experiment with tools and materials used in making paper pleated decoration for beauty and self-fulfillment.
KEY INQUIRIES QUESTION
  Where do we find pleated paper decorations in our environment?
  How do pleated paper decoration look like?

  Which colors would you want to use on your pleated paper item?

Review the previous lesson.
